reviews.title_excerpt: UI use errors from unconfirmed destructive actions, silent error swallowing, and accessibility barriers
additional_controls_required: Add automated axe-core CI gate for all routes (currently asserted manually for 20+ components)
Add explicit aria-live announcement when ConfirmDialog opens via keyboard shortcut so AT users hear the gate
Schedule annual independent WCAG 2.2 AA audit by external accessibility specialist (NHS Digital DCB0129 evidence)
reviews.rationale: Existing controls (ConfirmDialog gates, error surfacing, semantic landmarks, aria-current, skip-nav, AA contrast, aria-labels, error boundaries, .cursor/rules/ui-safety.mdc) directly address WCAG 2.2 AA SCs and IEC 62366-1 use-error principles. Detectability for AT users improves to 2 because confirm dialogs are now announced. Residual probability is remote because the cursor rule blocks regression at edit time. Independent annual audit recommended to satisfy NHS Digital accessibility statement obligations and Equality Act 2010 reasonable adjustment evidence.

reviews.title_excerpt: Graph algorithm results misinterpreted and acted on clinically without understanding data limitations
additional_controls_required: CoverageBadge amber state must encode the warning by icon + text in addition to colour (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color) so colour-blind users perceive it
Add visible focus state and aria-describedby linking the headline to the CoverageBadge so screen reader users hear coverage before the result
Verify Method Explainer disclosure pattern is keyboard-operable and announces expanded/collapsed state (aria-expanded)
Confirm Flesch-Kincaid <= 6 (age 9-11) on amber caution copy and headline output, not only <= 9
reviews.rationale: CoverageBadge, data-gating, and Method Explainer are well designed for sighted, statistically-naive users but rely on amber colour cues and visual reading order. WCAG 1.4.1 (colour alone) and 1.3.1 (programmatic relationship between badge and headline) are not yet evidenced. Health literacy controls reference FK <= 9 (per glossary CI gate) but the project rule (health-literacy.mdc) targets reading age 9-11, which corresponds to FK grade <= 6 / Flesch >= 60. Reading-level gap must be tightened before patient-reachable surfaces can be marked acceptable.

reviews.title_excerpt: Algorithm terminology in UI causes users to misinterpret findings and take incorrect action
affected_user_groups: patients (if any pathway result is patient-reachable)
additional_controls_required: Wire GlossaryTerm into Pathway Explorer column headers so unavoidable technical references (in Method Explainer) are explained on first hover/focus
Add a snapshot test that asserts headline_generator output Flesch >= 60 (not only <=9 grade) to align with health-literacy.mdc
reviews.rationale: Plain-English-only headlines, mapped column headers, and the headline_generator single source of truth meet WCAG 3.1.3/3.1.4 by avoiding jargon in primary surfaces. Method Explainer is a deliberate progressive disclosure (good pattern). Residual minor probability remains because new missions added later could bypass the lookup table; suggested glossary integration closes that gap.

reviews.title_excerpt: Low-contrast text or motion in UI leads to missed safety information
affected_user_groups: users with low vision / age-related macular degeneration
additional_controls_required: Add WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured assertion to Playwright sweep (new in WCAG 2.2)
Verify CONTRAST_PAIR test covers non-text UI components (1.4.11) at 3:1 not just text
Document a mechanism for patient-reachable user-generated HTML (e.g. imported PDF) so users can request a high-contrast re-render
reviews.rationale: Design tokens guaranteeing >=16px body, >=12px chip/caption, AA contrast, >=3px focus ring at >=3:1, prefers-reduced-motion, plus axe-core CI gate cover the bulk of WCAG 2.2 AA visual SCs. WCAG 2.2 introduces SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured which is not yet evidenced in CI. User-generated HTML edge case (PDF imports) retains residual risk; an explicit user-controlled re-render path is needed for full Equality Act 2010 reasonable adjustment cover.

reviews.title_excerpt: Dense UI causes mis-taps on patient-reachable screens
additional_controls_required: Confirm WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) 24x24 CSS px is asserted in CI for the Comfortable density tier (the >=44 assertion covers Spacious)
Ensure 'I am worried' and 'I understand' patient-reachable buttons are separated by >=24 px gutter and place the irreversible/escalating action with extra spacing (Hick's law + Fitts's law)
Visually invert the default order so 'I understand' is not adjacent to NHS 111 escalation (mis-tap mitigation)
Add patient usability evidence for under-16s and >75s in the quarterly mis-tap test cohort
reviews.rationale: Three-tier density with Spacious default >=44x44 px on patient routes plus Playwright assertion meets WCAG 2.5.5 (Enhanced 44x44) and exceeds the WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 Minimum (24x24). Residual risk is the spatial adjacency of escalation vs confirm controls (Fitts's-law mis-tap), which is a layout pattern issue not solved by target size alone. Spacing/order recommendation is a design-time control.

reviews.title_excerpt: Assistive-technology users cannot perceive navigation state or status information
affected_user_groups: blind / low-vision users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, ZoomText)
additional_controls_required: Schedule monthly NVDA + VoiceOver manual walkthrough that exercises ConfirmDialog, RoleSwitcher, and StatusDot patterns end-to-end
Add a status-change live region (aria-live=polite) for OrgSelect changes so AT users hear the new org context
Add a high-contrast / forced-colors mode test (Windows High Contrast / forced-colors media query) for AppShell
reviews.rationale: aria-current=page, button-as-button logo with aria-label, OrgSelect labelling, ConfirmDialog aria-labelledby/describedby, StatusDot shape+icon+colour, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, axe-core gate -- all map to the cited SCs. Detectability is best-case 1 for AT users because the AT itself surfaces the state. Residual risk lives in screens not yet migrated and forced-colors mode (Windows high-contrast) which is rarely audited.

reviews.title_excerpt: Patients and junior staff misunderstand clinical terms because jargon is not explained in-product
affected_user_groups: users with cognitive impairment / learning disability
users whose first language is not English (LEP)
additional_controls_required: Tighten readability gate from FK grade <=9 to FK grade <=6 (Flesch reading ease >=60) for all PATIENT-reachable copy, per health-literacy.mdc
Retain FK <=9 only for staff/clinician-only surfaces; document the split in the gate config
Add visible glossary-term affordance (dotted underline) discoverable without hover so keyboard and touch users notice the popover
Ensure GlossaryTerm popover is keyboard-dismissable (Escape) and focus returns to the trigger (WCAG 2.1.2)
Audit shipped copy against the health-literacy.mdc substitution table (e.g. 'haematuria' must offer 'blood in urine' on first use)
reviews.rationale: PageIntro, HelpPopover, CoachMark, ProgressiveReveal, GlossaryTerm primitives plus a readability CI gate are a strong pattern, but the gate threshold (FK <=9) corresponds to a US grade-9 reader (~age 14), not the 9-11 reading age mandated by health-literacy.mdc and the UK NHS readability convention (Flesch >=60). For patient-reachable copy this is a fail. Conditionally acceptable pending the FK <=6 split and glossary-term affordance work.

reviews.title_excerpt: Operations workspace misread by junior staff
additional_controls_required: Add aria-expanded to the four accordion section headers and ensure StatusDot text alternative is read together with section name by AT
Capture screenshot evidence of forced-colors mode for /admin/operations (Windows High Contrast)
Add a one-line role tooltip to 'Make it live' explaining that promotion is irreversible without a rollback (information for safety)
reviews.rationale: PageIntro at FK <=9 plus shape-encoded StatusDot covers the cited SCs for staff/operator audiences (not patient-reachable, so FK <=9 is appropriate). Residual risk is mostly forced-colors mode and AT announcement order on the four accordion headers; both are operational follow-ups rather than blocking gaps.

reviews.title_excerpt: Trainee misinterprets a coding-review case because clinical terms are not explained
affected_user_groups: users with dyslexia or low literacy
additional_controls_required: Suppress action must satisfy WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.6 Error Prevention (All) -- require explicit confirmation and provide a reverse/undo within 24h (already partially covered by ConfirmDialog gates)
Add a 'show example' link to GlossaryTerm popover for assertion vocabulary (declined / refuted / absent / planned / hypothetical) so trainees see a concrete clinical case
Track suppressions-rolled-back per trainee in the monitoring metrics already defined, to spot training gaps
reviews.rationale: PageIntro + GlossaryTerm + HelpPopover warning on suppress form provide layered explanation matching IEC 62366-1 information-for-safety controls. WCAG 3.1.3/3.1.4/3.1.5/3.3.2 satisfied for staff audience. WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.6 (new) requires reversible / checked / confirmed for irreversible writes -- already largely addressed by R-028 ConfirmDialog gate; cross-reference is sufficient.

reviews.title_excerpt: Role-scoped navigation hides a task the user needs to act on
affected_user_groups: screen reader users (Advanced tray collapsed by default)
additional_controls_required: Pending-count badges in Advanced tray must be announced by aria-live=polite when they change so AT users perceive the count rising without expanding the tray
RoleSwitcher must be reachable via skip-link or keyboard shortcut documented in the help (WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways)
Email/in-app banner copy for cross-role notifications must be FK <=9 and identify the assigned role explicitly ('You have a safety alert in your Staff inbox')
Ensure consistent navigation order across roles (WCAG 3.2.3) so muscle memory does not lead a multi-role user to the wrong area on switch
reviews.rationale: Always-visible RoleSwitcher and Advanced-tray pending counts are good design choices, plus role-agnostic backend notifications. Detectability stays at 3 for AT users because counts in a collapsed tray are not announced. aria-live and an explicit shortcut close the gap. Conditionally acceptable pending those AT enhancements.

reviews.title_excerpt: Animated transitions cause dizziness or nausea for users with vestibular disorders
affected_user_groups: users with vestibular disorders (BPPV, Meniere's, vestibular migraine)
additional_controls_required: Provide an in-product motion toggle (independent of OS preference) for users on shared devices where the OS preference is set elsewhere
Document for users that LEO honours OS prefers-reduced-motion in an accessibility statement page
reviews.rationale: useMotion + matchMedia + change-event subscription gives WCAG 2.3.3 conformance and immediate take-effect on toggle. Adding an in-product toggle is a defence-in-depth control for shared/public devices.

reviews.title_excerpt: Switching role mid-task discards unsaved safety-critical input
affected_user_groups: users with cognitive load (interrupted by phone/page)
screen reader users (focus must return to dialog)
additional_controls_required: Dirty-form confirmation dialog must trap focus, default to Cancel, and announce as a role=alertdialog with aria-describedby pointing at the unsaved-data summary
Provide an auto-draft to local storage so even if the user confirms switch, the half-written safety-net note is recoverable from the original route
Add an audit-log surfaced UI hint after role switch ('You had unsaved input on Suspected Cancer alert -- restore?') so the original task is not lost
reviews.rationale: Dirty-form confirm + append-only RoleSwitch audit + feature flag rollout match WCAG 3.3.4/3.3.6 and IEC 62366-1 use-error principles. Residual risk is the case where the user deliberately confirms switch and then forgets -- auto-draft + return-prompt closes the loop without blocking the deliberate action.

reviews.title_excerpt: Users lose access to admin reference pages because bookmarked links break when /admin/clinical is removed
affected_user_groups: users who rely on bookmarks (cognitive accommodation)
users with motor impairment (re-typing URLs is costly)
users with dyslexia (re-finding pages by browsing is costly)
screen reader users (re-orienting on a 404 is costly)
additional_controls_required: Custom 404 page (services/ui/.../not-found.tsx) should suggest the new /admin/knowledge?tab=<k> URL using a fuzzy match on the requested path -- defence-in-depth if a 308 is missed
Communicate the URL change in the in-product changelog so users update their personal bookmark notes
reviews.rationale: HTTP 308 permanent redirects + admin-url-audit Jest test fully address the cited SCs. Residual usability friction is one click of disorientation, addressed by a smarter 404 fallback.

reviews.title_excerpt: Users miss required information or take wrong action because Knowledge intro copy is unclear or missing for their role
affected_user_groups: users new to ConText negation rules
additional_controls_required: Pin the IntroCard headings as h2 inside the tab panel so screen reader users can navigate by heading
Where IntroCard refers to ConText / negation rules, link out to GlossaryTerm popovers rather than assume prior knowledge
Add a visible 'last reviewed' date so users know the role-aware copy is current
reviews.rationale: Per-role IntroCard copy + FK <=9 CI gate + role coverage gate + QA review meet WCAG 3.1.x/3.3.2 for the admin/knowledge audience (admin/knowledge is staff-only, so FK <=9 is the appropriate bar). Residual minor probability addressed by glossary linking and reviewed-date cue.

reviews.title_excerpt: Unified /work queue could mask a source that is piling up, delaying safety-net or coding action
affected_user_groups: screen reader users (counts strip vs list)
users on small viewports (counts strip must remain visible)
additional_controls_required: Counts-by-source strip must encode each source via icon + label, not colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1)
SLA colour band on SafetyNetAlert rows must include a non-colour cue (icon, text band, or pattern) for colour-blind detectability
Counts strip must update via aria-live=polite so AT users hear when SafetyNetAlert volume rises
Add a per-source filter chip set so a user can quickly isolate SafetyNetAlert when concerned
On viewports under 600 CSS px, ensure the counts strip remains pinned (sticky) and reflows without horizontal scroll (WCAG 1.4.10)
reviews.rationale: Counts-by-source + SLA colour band + retained source escalation are sound aggregator design, but accessibility detail (colour-only encoding, no aria-live, viewport behaviour) needs explicit SC mapping to be acceptable. Conditionally acceptable pending the four enhancements; risk is minor severity, so workshop accepts a remediation plan rather than blocking.

reviews.title_excerpt: Job status not surfaced or incorrect (FMEA-086 async job status)
affected_user_groups: screen reader users (need aria-live for async status)
keyboard-only users (must reach status without mouse)
users with cognitive impairment (need clear success/failure messaging)
users on slow connections (need progress feedback)
additional_controls_required: Async job status panel must use role=status (aria-live=polite) for in-progress updates and role=alert (aria-live=assertive) for failure
Provide both a polling fallback and a visible 'Last updated HH:MM' timestamp so users (and AT users) know when status was last refreshed
If polling fails, show an explicit 'Status check failed -- last known state was X at Y' rather than going silent (avoids the R-028 silent failure pattern)
Provide a manual 'Retry status check' button reachable by keyboard
Document expected job duration in PageIntro at FK <=9 so users do not assume a long job has stalled
reviews.rationale: FMEA-086 (Service Bus events not published or polling broken) is a Class A reliability item but has direct accessibility consequences: AT users rely on status messages they can hear. Without aria-live and a visible last-updated stamp, screen reader users do not perceive job state changes and may assume completion or failure incorrectly. Conditionally acceptable pending the role=status / role=alert + retry + last-updated work.

user_groups_most_impacted: patients and carers on touch devices
health_literacy_failures: R-LEO-AI-081 (patient-reachable copy gated at FK <=9 instead of <=6 / Flesch >=60 required by health-literacy.mdc for 9-11 reading age)
wcag_2_2_specific_gaps: SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) -- not yet asserted in CI (R-078)
SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) -- 24x24 px not asserted for Comfortable density tier (R-079)
SC 3.3.6 Error Prevention (All) -- partially covered by ConfirmDialog gates (R-028, R-083, R-091)
cross_cutting_recommendations: Split the Flesch-Kincaid CI gate: FK <=6 / Flesch >=60 for patient-reachable copy, FK <=9 for staff/clinician copy
Add forced-colors mode (Windows High Contrast) verification to the axe-core sweep
Schedule annual independent WCAG 2.2 AA audit by external accessibility specialist (NHS Digital DCB0129 evidence)
Standardise aria-live usage across async status surfaces (jobs, counts strips, dynamic counts)
Ensure non-text status encoding (icon + shape + colour) on all StatusDot, SLA-band, and CoverageBadge instances
